subject: EVS
central_question: How does the Godavari’s journey show the ways a river supports life, culture and livelihoods while also facing dams, pollution, floods and water scarcity?
in_scope_units: Where I Begin, Where I Flow: source, tributaries, route, length and destination of the Godavari.
Map reading: states, dams, wildlife areas and tributaries.
Sacred and cultural connections: Dakshina Ganga, Nashik and Godavari Pushkaram.
The Life I Hold: perennial and seasonal rivers, forests, wildlife, delta and Coringa Mangrove Forests.
The Many Ways I Support Lives and Activity 1: domestic water, irrigation, factories, livelihoods and ecotourism.
Dams—Storing My Water, Changing My Flow: reservoirs, benefits, flooding and displacement.
What Pollutes Me and Activities 2–4: waste, plastic, cleaners, dissolving substances and fertiliser-driven green blankets.
When a River Floods and Activities 5–7: impacts, safety tips and emergency role-play.
When a River Runs Dry: shortage, migration and effects on people and animals.
National Water Mission, water ATMs and daily water-saving actions.
Let us reflect, Questions 1–8: local rivers, culture, rules, filters and city planning.
banned_topics: General water cycle and aquatic adaptations from Chapter 1.
Food preservation and microbes from Chapter 3.
School waste and fire safety from Chapter 4.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Godavari begins as a large river at the coast.
known_pitfalls.correction: It begins as a stream at Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats and grows as tributaries join.
Dams store useful water but can flood land and displace people and animals.

known_pitfalls.claim: Clear-looking river water is always safe.
known_pitfalls.correction: Dissolved chemicals or dirty water may remain hidden.

known_pitfalls.claim: Walking through shallow-looking floodwater is safe.
known_pitfalls.correction: Activity 6 says not to walk or drive in floodwater and to move to higher ground.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT map questions: trace states, tributaries, dams and wildlife areas.
NCERT Activity 1: make a poster of river benefits.
NCERT Activity 3: compare sugar and cooking oil in water.
NCERT Activity 4: analyse a clean river and a green blanket.
NCERT Activity 5: match flood problems with affected needs.
NCERT Activity 6: organise actions before, during and after a flood.
NCERT Activity 7: role-play local leadership for flood safety.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter section is ‘Let us reflect’, Questions 1–8 on page 37.
